downside.story: P10: FTTH customers cut FY28 builds ~32% (not 15%) as AT&T/Verizon reprioritize FWA and overbuilders stay stopped; DCI ramps 25% slower; BEAD and copper slip; AI capex follows the file's low case and the DMV pauses stretch past mid-2027 so Building Systems is roughly flat; under-absorbed crews and customer credit losses take margins ~150bp lower; P/E stays ~8.7x as the market treats FY27 as the peak.

base.story: FY27 revenue $7.74B (just above the guide); FY28 $8.26B (Comms +4.5% with FTTH -15% offset by DCI, copper and BEAD; Building Systems +14.5% after a 3% moratorium haircut); FY29 $9.02B; adjusted EPS ~17.15 / 18.96 / 22.13 vs pre-print Nasdaq consensus 15.89 / 18.99 / 22.37. upside.story: P90: FTTH plans set in Q4 come in near flat, DCI awards keep doubling, BEAD and copper ramp on time, Building Systems grows ~28% with AI capex near the high case and the pauses lifting, Comms margin returns to 13%+ EBITDA, and the P/E recovers toward 13.5x.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's findings changed five things. (1) Tax: the P/E leg runs on adjusted EPS, so it takes the company-stated 26.0% non-GAAP rate (src 29; Q3 adjusted 25.3%) instead of GAAP history 23.5% (about -3%). (2) Exit multiple on one date and one vintage: peers at 2026-11-24 closes and 2026-11-25 Zacks consensus give a whole-company median of 14.55x (MTZ 13.0x, PRIM 11.95x, MYRG 16.1x, PWR 30.2x), not 17.1x at 2026-11-02 prices; STRL moves to segment-only; own 10.2x; k=0.8 -> 11.0x (was 11.3x). EV/EBITDA: 12.35x peer median, own 8.2x -> 8.2x. (3) Supplier finance: 204.4 of the 524.0 program (the excess over the FY26 year-end balance scaled by revenue) is treated as debt. (4) FTTH share: the 9M arithmetic (Comms +17% YTD = ~+701 with FTTH +50%, src 4) does not fit 31%: solving it gives FY26 FTTH ~1,650 and FY27 ~2,320 (~38%); FY28 -15% (-348, the same dollar cut as round 1) keeps FY28 Comms at +4.5%, inside 'mid-single-digit', and FY29 +8% (CEO: accelerating). I keep FTTH below the supervisor's 44% because DCI, copper and M&O also grew in 9M. (5) DMV moratoria (Loudoun pause adopted 2026-11-18, Maryland county pauses; src 30, 31): new legislative applications are held, by-right and under-construction work continues, so I haircut Building Systems 3% in FY28 and 5% in FY29 on top of the labor cap (FY28 +14.5%, below 'high teens or better'). Q4 FY27 is now built just above the guide (1,715) from Q3 momentum; it moves value only through net debt. Result: adjusted EPS ~17.15 / 18.96 / 22.13 (within 1% of pre-print consensus for FY28-29), research target (12m) $235.93 (was $252.17): P/E 228.35 (0.75), EV/EBITDA 258.69 (0.25). Scenarios keep the playbook's drivers (FTTH, DCI, copper/BEAD, Building Systems capture, margin, multiple): P10 $116.84, P90 $362.51. Where I differ from the supervisor's set (273.65 on 13.0x): I reprice the exit at today's price because the peers' own prices and consensus moved too, and the k rule is about the current gap. Research limited to ~6 new queries.

drivers.label: Fiber-to-the-home revenue (Communications)
drivers.source: Q3 FY27 call (CEO): FTTH up 50% through Q3; FY28 FTTH down vs FY27 but above FY26; AT&T 2027-28 capex lowered to $22-23B; Verizon shifting incremental coverage to FWA
drivers.derivation: FY26 not disclosed. Rebuilt on the 9M arithmetic (supervisor): CEO 'Communications ... up 17% year-to-date' and 'fiber-to-the-home revenue up 50% through Q3' (src 4). 9M FY27 Comms ~4,827 (YTD revenue 6,027.0 less Building Systems ~1,200) vs 9M FY26 ~4,126 (=4,827/1.17): +701. Non-FTTH 9M: DCI +75, copper +20, base -1% (wireless roll-off offset by M&O). 701 = 0.5 x F9 + 95 - 0.01 x (4,001 - F9) -> 9M FY26 FTTH F9 = 1,267; Q4 FY26 (14 weeks) ~383 -> FY26 1,650 (30% of FY26 Comms). FY27: 9M 1,900 + Q4 ~420 (moderation begins; CEO 'several large customers to moderate the pace') = 2,320 (+41%, 38% of FY27 Comms). Round 1's 1,250/1,850 (31%) left only ~460 of the 701 9M growth to FTTH and was inconsistent with a shrinking base, so it is withdrawn. FY28 -15% to 1,972 (-348): inside the CEO band (above FY26 1,650, below FY27), sized from AT&T's lowered 2027-28 capital investment (src 12) and Verizon routing incremental coverage to FWA (src 13); the dollar cut matches round 1 (-340). FY29 +5%: AT&T 60M locations by 2030 (src 12). Alternatives: supervisor's 44% share with -10% (-267, src 4 arithmetic with all growth to FTTH) and agent-style -20% (-464 on this base); see variant.
drivers.why: Largest and most volatile comms demand driver; the FY28 downturn is the thesis debate
drivers.variant_view: All 9M growth assigned to FTTH (44% share, FY27 ~2,670) and a -10% cut gives FY28 FTTH ~2,400: about +$9/share; -25% (customers cut as hard as AT&T's FY24 pause) about -$9/share.
